subject: Social Studies
title: Far from the beach
learningTarget: I can tell which physical region of Texas a place is in.
lessonSummary: Students sort Texas places into the Coastal Plains or the Mountains and Basins. The trap is going by how a place looks instead of where it is. Page 2 adds places in the other two regions.
trap: Thinking the Coastal Plains is only land by the beach, and that any place with cliffs belongs in the mountains.

pages.rule: Sort by the region each place is in.
pages.notThis: A region is huge. One photo does not show the whole region.

mc.prompt: Dallas is hundreds of miles from the beach. Why is it in the Coastal Plains?

choices.text: The Coastal Plains reaches far inland from the coast.
Because it is a big city, like Houston.
Because it sits on the Rio Grande.

multi.prompt: Choose all that are true about the Mountains and Basins.

choices.text: It is in far West Texas.
It has the highest point in Texas.
Every place in it is a mountain.

defs.text: A large, mostly flat region in the east and south of Texas. It reaches far inland from the coast.
The region in far West Texas. It has mountains, with low, flat basins between them.
A large, mostly flat region in the east and south of Texas. It reaches far inland from the coast.
The region in far West Texas. It has mountains, with low, flat basins between them.
It is in one of the other two regions: the Great Plains or the North Central Plains.
A large, mostly flat region in the east and south of Texas. It reaches far inland from the coast.
The place sits on the river that forms the border between Texas and Mexico.
